card: Allows importing public-key-only descriptors into wallets with private keys enabled when the wallet already possesses the corresponding private keys. Previously, Bitcoin Core rejected public descriptors on privkey-enabled wallets, requiring private keys to be exposed and re-entered in RPC calls. The wallet now inspects existing ScriptPubKeyMans for matching keys, substituting origin-annotated xpubs (including within musig expressions) with known master xprvs. Closes issue #27336.
changed_since_previous: Added key extraction and substitution support for participants in musig() descriptor expressions, and base PR #34861 was merged.
evidence: Closes issue #27336 ('Should be able to import an xpub descriptor to a privkey-enabled wallet if the wallet has the privkeys')

Author notes in PR description: 'Currently importing a descriptor to a wallet that has private keys requires the descriptor to include the private keys. This is not ideal as it means exposing private key material.'
problem: Importing a public descriptor into a private-key-enabled wallet fails unless the descriptor explicitly contains private keys. Users are forced to export and expose sensitive private keys via RPC even when the wallet already possesses the corresponding master xprv or single keys.

risk.why: A flaw in derivation path concatenation or key substitution during import could corrupt wallet descriptors or associate wrong signing keys, leading to generating unspendable addresses or loss of funds.

summary: Allows importing descriptors lacking private keys into private-key-enabled wallets when the wallet already holds those keys. The wallet inspects existing ScriptPubKeyMans for matching private keys and master xprvs, substitutes them into origin-annotated xpubs (including participants inside musig expressions), and adds matching individual private keys to the import keyset.
